draft.title: Carbohydrates
card: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy. The body breaks them down into glucose, which cells use as fuel.
Simple
sugars that are broken down quickly, so they release energy fast. Examples are the sugars in lollies and soft drink.
Complex
starches that take longer to break down, so they release energy slowly. Examples are wholegrain bread, oats, brown rice and legumes.
Fibre
a part of plant foods that the body does not break down for energy. It helps digestion and keeps bowel movements regular.
draft.remember: Carbohydrates fuel the body. Complex ones and fibre give steady energy and help digestion.

a.q: Which food is the best source of a slow release of energy?
opts: A bowl of rolled oats
A glass of soft drink
A handful of jelly lollies
A cup of fruit juice with added sugar
a.why: Oats are a complex carbohydrate, which takes longer to break down, so energy is released slowly. Soft drink is mostly simple sugar, which is broken down quickly and gives fast energy.
a.clue: Look for the starchy whole food, not the sugary one.

b.q: Tom eats a wholegrain sandwich with salad at lunch. Mia eats a bag of lollies. Which statement best compares them?
opts: Tom's lunch gives slower energy and fibre for digestion
Tom's lunch gives no energy because it has fibre
Mia's lollies give slower energy than Tom's lunch
Mia's lollies give more fibre than Tom's lunch
b.why: Wholegrain bread is a complex carbohydrate and the salad adds fibre, so energy is released slowly and digestion is helped. Fibre is not broken down for energy, but the bread still supplies energy, so the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Fibre helps digestion, but the bread is still a fuel.

b.best: Tom's lunch gives slower energy and fibre for digestion
